THE PREAMBLE, verbatim:
## Slice two units

One row is one PR, from main, signed and through the merge queue after the
operator rules. Follow this order. Dependencies are semantic prerequisites,
not simply the preceding row; the independence of U1–U4 is explicit in D9.
No row through U9a lifts the MCP compile fence. U9b is the sole enabling PR.
The lettered splits are required by the checked seams: record schema plus
embedded copy already consumes two files; multi-server wiring crosses runtime,
protocol and adapter data; storage/folding/inspect crosses CLI, protocol,
runtime and pure view. Minimal ledger writing is deliberately pulled into U6.

`contracts/realms.v<N>.schema.json` denotes one exact future file allocated
as **the next realms version after v7** at U5c, including v7's fields. It is
the only intentionally deferred filename number. Every other production path
below is literal. New paths are proposed modules/schemas, not files created
by this document plan. Constructors/registration are counted in their row.
Future tests extend the named suites; capability_broker already exists under
the consolidated CLI integration binary. New capability_artifacts and runtime
capability_ledger/capability_broker_launch modules are registered through the
existing test-only roots (CLI tests/it.rs and runtime tests/it.rs), not new
undeclared binaries. Tests may use child modules of the owning suites to stay
below 2,000 lines; list every test move in unit evidence.

Each row closes exactly its numbered tasks, including tests/mutations and
gate evidence. Test lists below are the allowed owning suites; every row
also updates this change's tasks and later implementation evidence. Measured
witness/compose pins accompany only rows that change their inputs.

YOUR ROW, verbatim:
| U7d2 | U7d | Seal the brokered server set after provisioning; 36.1–36.2 | `crates/brokkr-runtime/src/engine.rs`; `crates/brokkr-runtime/src/engine/broker.rs`; `crates/brokkr-runtime/src/engine/panel.rs`; `crates/brokkr-runtime/src/engine/sequence.rs`; `crates/brokkr-runtime/src/bundle/mcp.rs`; `crates/brokkr-protocol/src/native_controls/mcp.rs` |

YOUR UNIT, verbatim:
### U7d2 — Seal the brokered server set after provisioning

Thread each provisioned slot's `Pin` (locator and digest) and its dialect secret names out of the engine's provisioning in engine/broker.rs, and seal them into `SealedServers::Brokered`: each `SealedBroker` carries its capability, plan locator, plan digest and removals, from the holding's brokered marks. A single seat's serving inputs are sealed after its plans are provisioned, as panels and sequence steps already order it, and panels and sequence steps seal the same pins. The intent the engine reads (`McpIntent`) gains the brokered case; the MCP compile fence stays. engine.rs is frozen at its baseline; new private child modules beside it follow the standing rule. No public API change.

Split from U7d (operator ruling 2026-10-16): the first U7d run found no engine producer of a brokered set.

Closes, with U7d and U7d3, tasks 36.1 and 36.2; requirements [MB1](specs/mcp-capability-broker/spec.md), [MB4](specs/mcp-capability-broker/spec.md), [SI2](specs/strict-mcp-isolation/spec.md).
Proof: Actual engine-composed cold, resume and replacement commands carry hands plus brokers that match independent literal server intent, and a mutated pin, plan digest or removal refuses at the final serving boundary. A seat with no brokered mark seals no broker; native and no-MCP launches and the requested-effect digest are unchanged. Bind each with a compiling removal.

Operator rulings 2026-10-16, after U7d2's first run parked (0065-slice-two-unit-u7d2-see-the-0f821977, IMPL-OVERSIZED-EXHAUSTED, no commit): the engine writes a site's hands document into its argv through `Transport::expand`, which is hands-only, and the whole-set builder (`Servers::expand`, `Transport::beside`) is private to brokkr-protocol, so a brokered seal beside a hands-only argv refuses at the final serving boundary. U7d2's row gains `crates/brokkr-protocol/src/native_controls/mcp.rs` for one public whole-set expansion of a measured hands fragment beside sealed brokers through the set's one builder (for example `Transport::expand_beside(fragment, brokers)`). Hands-only callers keep their output byte for byte, and no second builder of the MCP document exists in brokkr-runtime. The public API rise this needs is approved as measured, up to +3 lines of quality/public-api/brokkr-protocol.txt; a larger rise comes back to the operator. A single seat's hands segment is expanded beside its attempt's provisioned brokers after provisioning and before its spawn is sealed, as panel members and sequence steps already order it. The session question still asks of the command composed before the durable start; the instance key reads the selection's argv (`argv_for`), not the expanded document, so attempt-specific plan locators never enter it. A new private child of engine.rs (such as engine/isolation.rs) and the existing child engine/marks.rs follow the standing rule.

Owning tests: `crates/brokkr-runtime/src/engine/capability_tests.rs`, `crates/brokkr-runtime/src/engine/resume_tests.rs`, `crates/brokkr-runtime/tests/capability_launch.rs`.

CONTROLLER'S STATE FOR THIS RUN (the-forge-67, 2026-10-16). This is a RE-VOUCH of U7d2's PR #721, not a new implementation.
- U7d2's second run (0065-slice-two-unit-u7d2-see-the-2dc6ea4e) judged 07cbfcbe on 1d0d47e4: REVIEW-RESIDUAL-OK (F1, F2 low; F3–F5 info). The operator's ruling widened the row by crates/brokkr-protocol/src/native_controls/mcp.rs and approved the public API rise as measured up to +3; it measured 1162 → 1163.
- PR CI then failed two required checks, and the controller fixed both in brokered_tests.rs ONLY, signed commit c9ddc885:
  (1) Exact coverage counted 7,483 of 7,484 functions. The uncalled one was serving_inputs' map_err closure in engine/isolation.rs, since the engine seals through `served` and only the public entry renders `Unsealed` as text. a_broker_set_that_is_not_the_provisioned_one_refuses_its_spawn now also seals the brokering site through the public serving_inputs and asserts its exact Unprovisioned refusal. Altering the closure's text fails it at brokered_tests.rs:734.
  (2) macOS failed an_attempt_directory_that_is_not_utf8_seals_no_broker: APFS refuses non-UTF-8 names with EILSEQ. That test is now #[cfg(target_os = "linux")].
- Main then moved: #716 (recipe shelf, runtime places.rs, runtime API listing) and #719 (bundle.rs, parse.rs, tier.rs, new bundle/opened.rs, quality suppressions and too-many-lines). The branch was rebased onto e929ae90 with no conflicts; cargo check passes.

Gates: runtime --lib, --test capability_launch and --test it; protocol --lib; workspace clippy -D warnings; fmt; typos; openspec validate --all --strict; quality/ratchet.sh files, clones and api. Add a short "Re-vouch" paragraph to evidence/U7d2.md.

STANDING RULINGS. Decision 0065's hold: off by default, no grandfathering; realm-only grants; tools are an abstraction, dialects the concrete; refuse, never reconcile (slice one's operator ruling of 2026-09-23). The MCP compile fence stays in place until U9b. Hosts are Linux and macOS only (decision 0063). Main's code-health rules bind: no `unsafe` in brokkr-runtime; `#[expect(.., reason)]`, never `#[allow]`; clippy's too_many_lines, excessive_nesting and struct_excessive_bools are denied, so split, and only if splitting would widen your unit carry `reason = "baseline 2026-09-29, decision 0065 slice one merged with main; split after #319"`; when a count moves, re-measure quality/'s file-lines, too-many-lines and suppressions (the steps quality/measure.sh uses), witness pins with `BROKKR_BLESS=1 cargo test -p brokkr-runtime --test witness_digests` (or, once #423's single test binary is on your base — crates/brokkr-runtime/tests/it.rs exists — `BROKKR_BLESS=1 cargo test -p brokkr-runtime --test it witness_digests::`), and budgets with scripts/measure-budgets.sh. Where a crate has tests/it.rs, a NEW tests/*.rs file must be registered as `mod <file>;` in that crate's tests/it.rs (layering::test_targets refuses an unregistered one), unless it sets HOME, cwd, env or a global allocator, in which case it is its own [[test]] in Cargo.toml with the reason written there; and `--test <file>` filters become `--test it <file>::` (capability_launch stays its own binary).

RULES. Touch at most the production files your row names; if the real scope exceeds them, STOP and report `oversized` with the split. One exception, the operator's standing rule of 2026-10-09 (operator-ruling-2026-10-03.md): beside a production file in your row that sits at its 800-line ceiling, or is frozen at its quality/file-lines.txt baseline above it, you may add NEW private child modules, declared from that file, in its own module tree and consumed in this unit, without stopping. The same holds beside a row file that your own change would push past 800 lines (extended 2026-10-11). You may also change an EXISTING private child module of a file in your row, in that file's own module tree (extended 2026-10-11). You may move existing code out of the full file into such a child to make room, preferring the code your change touches. Name each new file in your evidence and commit, and set its quality/file-lines.txt row. You may also add a name to an EXISTING re-export in the parent module that declares one of your row's files, where the parent's line count does not change (extended 2026-10-10). Files in any other module tree still mean `oversized`; any public API growth still needs the operator's ruling at PR time (record it, do not stop). Test files are NOT bounded by the row (controller's standing clarification, 2026-10-05): a test anywhere that pins behaviour your unit changes, a validator or fixture swap in another suite, or a new child test module beside an owning suite that sits over its line ceiling is part of your unit — size-neutral wherever a file sits at its quality/file-lines.txt baseline. A LOW finding you cannot fix inside your row's production files: record it in your result and do NOT report blocked for it. Tests assert exact reasons and values, never is_err(); every new test is bound by a compiling mutation that makes it fail, then restored, recorded (test, assertion) in evidence.md. Tick a task in tasks.md only on observed evidence; record results in a NEW file of your own, openspec/changes/decision-0065-capabilities-slice-two/evidence/U7d2.md (two lanes deliver units at once, and every unit appending to evidence.md made each pair of pull requests conflict), and do not edit evidence.md itself; write it in prose or a table — never as a bullet list of the standard gate lines (`cargo fmt ...: clean`, `cargo clippy ...: clean`), which earlier evidence files already hold word for word, so the data clone gate refuses it; never edit the tasks.md preamble. Fixtures build on a canonicalised temporary root; no test reads .forge/ or needs an installed provider. Frozen contracts, policy/phase-machine.json, fixtures/, reference/ and extensions/ do not move unless your unit names them. Sign every commit (`git commit -S`; main requires signatures). HEADLESS SEAT: your session ends the moment you end a turn — never run a command in the background, never use Monitor or ScheduleWakeup, run every command in the foreground under the tool's 10-minute limit (suites crate by crate with `timeout 590`, split by --lib/--test if longer), and write your result file before you finish. GATES: cargo fmt --all -- --check; cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings; the suite of each crate you touched; openspec validate --all --strict; typos --hidden; git diff --check; quality/ratchet.sh files and clones. CI also builds and tests on macOS, which this host cannot: Linux-only code (namespaces, mountinfo, /proc, device numbers, Linux-only syscalls) goes behind `#[cfg(target_os = "linux")]` with a non-Linux stand-in that refuses, as broker/session.rs does, and any libc or rustix type you use must be the same type on both (rustix's Dev is u64 on Linux and i32 on macOS; U6c6a's first PR failed to compile there). Keep the session small; commit when the unit is done; never push.

instructions.analyze:
# OpenSpec analyze

Judge duplication, ambiguity, underspecification, house alignment, coverage gaps, and inconsistency across proposal, deltas, design and tasks. Treat the realm house as the constitution. Return each finding with severity and its earliest owning artifact; zero findings is consistent.

Judge underspecified areas, unquantified language, missing decisions, capability/delta mismatches, and requirements without adequate scenarios. Return every ambiguity with the evidence needed to settle it; zero findings is clear.
instructions.design:
# OpenSpec design

Write `openspec/changes/<change>/design.md`. Record context, goals and non-goals, decisions with alternatives, risks, migration, and open questions. On return, revise the design and dependent artifacts so no finding is merely acknowledged.

# OpenSpec return

Revise the returned change in dependency order. Encode an answered ambiguity as a scenario, record design choices under `## Decisions`, and keep every dependent artifact coherent. Record a reasoned refusal in the owning artifact.

Revise the returned change in dependency order. Encode an answered ambiguity as a scenario, record design choices under `## Decisions`, and keep every dependent artifact coherent. Record a reasoned refusal in the owning artifact.

Change location: `openspec/changes/{change}`. Archive operation: ["openspec","archive","{change}","--yes"].

# OpenSpec archive

Folding a change is the last task: run the archive operation named above,
which moves the change directory under `openspec/changes/archive/` and
folds its deltas into `openspec/specs/`. Folding also records which change
wrote which capability, so every capability the change touched carries a
`## Provenance` list.

After the archive operation, open each capability's
`openspec/specs/<capability>/spec.md` that the change touched and append
exactly one line under a `## Provenance` heading held at the end of the
file:

`- \`<archived-directory-name>\` — folded <YYYY-MM-DD>`

`<archived-directory-name>` is the directory the archive operation
created under `openspec/changes/archive/`; `<YYYY-MM-DD>` is the day it
was folded. Append only: never rewrite, reorder or remove an existing
provenance line, because standing truth accumulates and is not edited into
a different meaning. The line is a pointer, not a summary — it names the
change and nothing else, and the why stays in the change directory.

house.content:
This realm is a Rust workspace. Production code is Rust under `crates/`; the
Rust-only architecture is recorded by decision 0009. Semantic changes carry a
decision document with status `proposed` because only the operator accepts one.
Intake seats read `README.md` and decisions 0004 and 0005 before framing a
commission, along with the code and history it touches.

The frozen v1 contracts under `contracts/`, the production table at
`policy/phase-machine.json`, and `reference/` (its schemas included) are
read-only.
A contract change lands as a new version file beside the old one, never as an
edit. The evaluator corpus under `fixtures/` is also frozen and is never
regenerated, only versioned.

Tests are part of every change. Extend the suite that proves the code, run
`cargo test --workspace`, compile `recipes/self`, and leave formatting, clippy,
and the exact-coverage gate clean before reporting success.

Commit completed work with `git` using the repository's message style. Never
push.

The supported hosts are Linux and macOS (decision 0063); WSL2 is Linux. Write
no Windows-conditional code, test or evidence.

## Architecture

Decision 0071 rules how code here is shaped. Build to it, and cite its ruling
numbers in what you judge. Where a gate named below holds a rule, the gate is
the authority, and a finding it would catch is the gate's.

- **Pure core (ruling 1).** `brokkr-core` and `brokkr-view` do no I/O and read
  no clock, environment or randomness. They run no process. Pass `now`, paths
  and environment in as arguments. Effects live in the crates above core and
  view, and are journaled.
- **Enums and data, not traits (ruling 2).** A closed set is an enum matched
  exhaustively, with no wildcard arm that decides behaviour. Anything an
  operator extends is data under `adapters/`, `agents/`, `recipes/` or
  `realms.json`, validated and digested. Add a trait only for a seam whose
  contract spans several operations that must stay consistent with one
  another, reached across a process or service boundary, and name that seam
  in its doc comment. `ProducerTransport` is the one such trait today. A test
  double alone does not make a seam: a single substitutable function is a
  closure seam (`*_with`, `*_in`), which is how the house inverts a
  dependency otherwise.
- **Typed at the edge (ruling 3).** Parse wire, file and harness data once
  into a type, with `serde` and `deny_unknown_fields` where the contract is
  closed. `serde_json::Value` never goes past the edge, into state, or back
  out by string key. Never put `format!("{:?}")` in anything digested or
  journaled. A doubly-optional field or a string vocabulary is a missing enum.
- **Small functions (ruling 4).** New and changed functions stay within 100
  lines, nesting depth 5 and 7 parameters. Cyclomatic complexity follows
  the operator's 2026-09-26 ruling: a function may reach the higher of 15
  and its baseline, so a new function stays within 15, an existing one may
  change freely up to 15, and one already over 15 may only shrink.
  Production files stay within 800 lines and test files within 2,000, and a
  file already over may not grow. Add no new `jscpd` clone in production
  code, test code or data. `quality/` holds the measured baseline. Today's
  offenders carry `#[allow(clippy::…)]`, and #337 converts them to
  `#[expect(clippy::…, reason = "…")]`. Add a suppression only by a ruling,
  and remove it when you fix the function. A new suppression is
  `#[expect(…, reason)]`, never `#[allow]`.
- **Once (ruling 5).** Every fact has one home. A repeated vocabulary, skeleton
  or helper becomes one function or one table. An agent is defined once under
  `agents/`, and seats hire it by reference. A recipe that differs from another
  by a model, a seat or an entry is an `extends` overlay, never a copy. The
  agent library does not yet accept `extends`, and #360 builds it. Until then,
  a variation of an agent lives at the seat that hires it, overridden in a
  recipe overlay. It is never a second agent file that restates the first. A
  copy that must exist, such as a script a bundle pins, is held to its source
  by a test.
- **Nothing unused (ruling 6).** Add no alias, agent, contract version, flag or
  `pub` item without a consumer, and prefer `pub(crate)`. A deprecation names
  the release that removes it.
- **One derivation (ruling 7).** A fact shown on two surfaces is derived once
  in `brokkr-view`. The CLI, the TUI and `ui.html` only paint it. The engine
  never admits anything by a display-crate function.
- **Typed errors (ruling 8).** Return a `thiserror` enum whose `Display` keeps
  the operator's text. Tests match variants and pin each module's text once.
  Add no new `Result<_, String>`.
- **Tests that bind (ruling 9).** Assert exact values or variants, never
  `is_err()` alone. Show that every new test binds: a compiling mutation that
  removes the behaviour must make it fail. Restore the behaviour and record
  the failing test. Share fixtures through builders. Never change the process
  environment without a guard that restores it on unwind. A production guard
  left out because the exact-coverage gate would count it unreachable carries
  a removal-control test for the invariant that makes it unreachable, and the
  comment explaining the omission names that test.
- **The house's patterns (ruling 10).**
  - A harness is a module behind `AdapterKind`. This is the target form;
    today all five kinds share one module, and #347 and #348 build the
    split.
  - A CLI verb is a `Cmd` variant plus a handler.
  - A long parameter list becomes a parameter object.
  - Argv and mount tables are built with a builder.
  - Observing the world is split from deciding on it.
  - Never use a trait-object registry for a closed set.

Judges rate a finding against these rulings by this table, and cite the ruling
number:

- **info:** something a house gate would catch. The gate's verdict is the
  authority.
- **low:** a new or changed function over a ceiling, a rule written a second
  time, an item added without a consumer, or a `Value` carried past its edge
  within one module.
- **medium:** an untyped vocabulary that crosses crates, recipe or agent data
  copied instead of extended, a fact derived a second time on another surface,
  an error matched by its text, or a new test that cannot fail.
- **high or above:** any violation that hides a fail-open path or weakens a
  refusal. It is carried as a security finding.

A principle the implementer bent knowingly, and named with its reason in
`notes`, is still rated, and the judge carries that reason with the finding.

## Release configuration

The release manager prepares the candidate and profile patches; the operator
publishes them. Local validation is preparation work. Remote CI on the final PR
head, publication, channel updates and live-profile verification are handoff
steps, recorded as pending until their remote results exist. Historical
"live from" channel versions and old journal examples are historical facts,
not current-version references to replace.

members.adversarial: Security review, adversarial stance, of U7d2's full net diff e929ae90..9fe2c220 (signed 9fe2c220, gpgsig present), read-only: no fixes, no commits. I re-derived the sealing path from the code rather than trusting the evidence, and found no fail-open path, no weakened refusal and no tamper path above info; security-hold is not warranted. INJECTION: the brokers are built only from what provisioning wrote (broker::written's Inventory pins and each Seal.secrets) and kept on Selection.brokers keyed by slot label. No seat result, driver output, protocol message or recipe value feeds capability, plan, digest or removals. Transport::expand_beside -> Servers::named/expand refuses an unbare or colliding cap- name, and capability must be bare before any document is built; the document is emitted with serde_json, so quote/brace breakout is impossible. isolation::beside matches the spawn's segment by full value against the measured fragment's hands-only expansion (never by length/search), rewrites only a lone Origin::Hands segment and leaves argv untouched on refusal (Unexpanded). An injected token in the spawn argv therefore never expands. FAIL-CLOSED: isolation::servers refuses (Unsealed::Unprovisioned) unless marks::brokered_at's brokered capabilities and Selection.brokers' provisioned capabilities name the same list in the same order, in both directions; the public mark_capabilities passes &[] and so refuses a brokered site instead of serving it hands-only, and a site holding none handed brokers refuses. A refusal sets spawn.refusal and no spawn occurs; verify_record/verify_serving still run at every spawn, and beside runs before spawn.seal so the expanded segments are what the launch record seals. SECRETS/JOURNAL: SealedBroker.removals are dialect secret NAMES (Implementation::Mcp.secrets), never values; launch_arguments and SERVING_INPUTS carry plan locators, digests and env-var names only. Neither object is appended to the journal: the EffectStarted payload is built separately, and site_plans/the session question read argv_for, not the expanded spawn, so attempt-specific locators enter no instance key or requested digest. TAMPER: a mutated plan locator or digest is refused at the dispatch door (strict decode/compare) and, past the door, at the harness final check (final_set/check_final); the broker re-verifies the plan digest on serve itself; a mutated removal is refused at the door; a non-UTF-8 locator is refused as Unprovisioned::Write before brokers()'s to_string_lossy runs, because serde's PathBuf serializer rejects invalid UTF-8. The provision() stand-in is #[cfg(test)] and thread-local, so it is absent from release and integration builds. The MCP compile fence is still Standing (Lifted is #[cfg(test)]). Public API: brokkr-protocol.txt is 1163 lines against main's 1162 (the single approved expand_beside line, inside the operator's +3), and brokkr-runtime.txt has no diff. I confirmed the only new protocol test passes here and cargo fmt --check is clean. INFO notes, not defects: (1) the non-UTF-8 removal control is cfg(linux) because APFS rejects such names, so macOS has no control for that guard (fail-closed regardless); (2) a removal list tampered past the dispatch door is not independently re-derived by the driver (U7d design, disclosed); (3) U7d2 activates dialect secret-name removals before U7d3's harness-authentication collision admission, but the standing fence keeps brokered launches unserved until U9b. Host limitation: on this box the 8 brokered runtime tests take the skip path ('no temporary directory here protects a HOME'), because / is owned by nobody here; I could not observe them execute, so that binding rests on the recorded CI/host run. This does not affect the security verdict.
